cohort_definitions.B_development: new; may be used to diagnose failures

assignment_rule: parity of sha256(site_id): even -> C, odd -> B (made before scoring)

sites.name: Atacama Desert, Chile

pairs.relationship: NASA Science: researchers collect soil samples in Chile's Atacama Desert to study conditions relevant to Mars; NASA lists Atacama among analog field sites.
NASA Science: researchers collect soil samples in Chile's Atacama Desert to study conditions relevant to Mars; NASA lists Atacama among analog field sites.

sources.label: NASA Science - Planetary Analogs

sites.limitations: NASA page states soil sampling for Mars-relevant dryness; says nothing about chloride deposits or Jezero geology specifically.

sites.name: Devon Island / Haughton crater, Canada

pairs.relationship: NASA-led Haughton-Mars Project: barren, freezing, isolated polar-desert terrain used to simulate Mars (and Moon) exploration.

sources.label: Mars Institute - Haughton-Mars Project (station coordinates 75 26 N, 89 52 W as reported by search)

sites.limitations: Impact-crater + polar desert; ice-rich permafrost but not Arcadia-style buried ice plains.

sites.name: Lava Beds National Monument, USA

pairs.relationship: NASA Science: researchers map lava tubes at Lava Beds National Monument with GPR, magnetometers and seismometers, linked to Moon and Mars.

sources.label: NASA Science - Planetary Analogs

sites.limitations: NASA page: mapping and detecting lava tubes; the subsurface property itself is invisible to a surface model.

sites.name: Kilauea volcano, Hawaii, USA

pairs.relationship: NASA analog missions page: Hawaii's Kilauea Volcano is a planetary analog site used to simulate Moon and Mars conditions.

sources.label: NASA - Analog Missions

sites.limitations: NASA: timing of geologist/astronaut tasks in volcanic terrain similar to the lunar surface; not a lava-tube analog statement.

sites.name: Icelandic volcanic fields

pairs.relationship: NASA: Iceland has served as a lunar stand-in for astronaut geology training since Apollo (1967), and the Artemis II crew trained there in 2024; both Iceland and the Moon feature basalts and breccias.

sources.label: Lunar lava tube base construction / terrestrial test-site reviews (as surfaced by search; specific attribution unverified)

sites.limitations: Geological style analog (Apollo-era training); no verified source in this project for lava tubes specifically.

sites.name: Death Valley, USA

pairs.relationship: NASA Science highlights drone and field tests in Death Valley as planetary-analog testing.
NASA Science highlights drone and field tests in Death Valley as planetary-analog testing.

sources.label: NASA Science - Planetary Analogs

sites.limitations: NASA page: drone testing for Martian sands and skies. Evaporite geology is general knowledge, not from that page.

sites.name: Colorado Desert, California, USA

pairs.relationship: NASA/JPL field-tested the ERNEST prototype rover in the Colorado Desert (March 2026) for future Moon (and possibly Mars) rovers.
NASA/JPL field-tested the ERNEST prototype rover in the Colorado Desert (March 2026) for future Moon (and possibly Mars) rovers.

sources.label: NASA/JPL field-tested the ERNEST prototype rover in the Colorado Desert (March 2026) for future Moon (and possibly Mars) rovers.

sites.limitations: Original v1 label; no specific source retained.

sites.name: McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica

pairs.relationship: NASA NTRS: the McMurdo Dry Valleys are the best-known Earth analog of the Martian high-northern plains where Phoenix landed (ground ice, permafrost, instrument testing); NASA Astrobiology describes Beacon and University Valley ice-cemented ground as Mars analogs.

sources.label: NASA NTRS: the McMurdo Dry Valleys are the best-known Earth analog of the Martian high-northern plains where Phoenix landed (ground ice, permafrost, instrument testing); NASA Astrobiology describes Beacon and University Valley ice-cemented ground as Mars analogs.

sites.limitations: Ground ice under dry permafrost is widely published as a Phoenix-site analog (search summary of Planetary & Space Science 2013 and others); this cell is mostly ice-sheet at 2.5 deg.

sites.name: Svalbard, Norway (AMASE)

pairs.relationship: NASA Goddard: the Arctic Mars Analogue Svalbard Expedition (AMASE) has tested flight-like Mars instruments and studied basaltic carbonates (ALH84001-like) at Svalbard sites since 2003.

sources.label: NASA Goddard: the Arctic Mars Analogue Svalbard Expedition (AMASE) has tested flight-like Mars instruments and studied basaltic carbonates (ALH84001-like) at Svalbard sites since 2003.

sites.limitations: Astrobiology field site (AMASE); relation to Jezero geology is thematic.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon National Monument, Idaho, USA

pairs.relationship: US National Park Service: Apollo 14 crew members visited in August 1969 to study volcanic geology (the NPS FAQ notes they did not formally train there); NASA Earth Observatory describes the lava landscape as lunar-like. Basaltic lava field with lava tubes.

US National Park Service: Apollo 14 crew members visited in August 1969 to study volcanic geology (the NPS FAQ notes they did not formally train there); NASA Earth Observatory describes the lava landscape as lunar-like. Basaltic lava field with lava tubes.

sources.label: Basaltic terrains in Idaho and Hawai'i as planetary analogs for Mars geology and astrobiology (Astrobiology 2019, as surfaced by search)

sites.limitations: BASALT: Mars basalt geology/astrobiology and operations. Its v2 mapping to Moon targets was our own mapping.

sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station area (San Rafael Swell), Utah, USA

pairs.relationship: NASA NTRS / NASA Astrobiology Institute reports describe the Morrison Formation area around MDRS as an analogue for Mars geomorphology and sedimentary processes (soil cores from the main geologic units).

sources.label: NASA NTRS / NASA Astrobiology Institute reports describe the Morrison Formation area around MDRS as an analogue for Mars geomorphology and sedimentary processes (soil cores from the main geologic units).

sites.limitations: Mars Desert Research Station: operational analog; geology is sedimentary desert.

sites.name: Gobustan / Caspian mud-volcano province
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Largest onshore concentration of mud volcanoes; sparse vegetation; semi-arid.

pairs.relationship: Earth region studied as morphologic and sedimentary analog of Martian cones/domes in Acidalia

sources.label: Allen & Oehler 2010, Mud Volcanoes - Analogs to Martian Cones and Domes (AGU abstract)

sites.limitations: Authors name Gulf of Cadiz submarine volcanoes as the closest morphologic analogs; land climate (semi-arid, warm) is unlike Acidalia. Match is geological, not climatic.

sites.name: Corona lava tube, Lanzarote
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Basaltic volcanic island; ~8 km lava tube mapped in 3D; hyperarid maritime climate.

pairs.relationship: Used by ESA PANGAEA/CAVES for planetary cave and lava-tube training and mapping

sources.label: ESA PANGAEA training programme (eoPortal)
Sauro et al. 2020, Lava tubes on Earth, Moon and Mars: a review (Earth-Science Reviews)

sites.limitations: Surface model sees basaltic climate only; tube geometry is invisible at 2.5 deg. Earth tubes are far narrower than lunar ones (Sauro et al.).

sites.name: Dalangtan playa, Qaidam Basin
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: High-altitude hyperarid evaporite basin: salt lakes, playas, sulfate/chloride-type salts, 20,000 km2 yardang fields.

pairs.relationship: Evaporite assemblages and polygonal salt crusts compared with Martian salt deposits
Yardang fields compared with Medusae Fossae-type wind erosion (yardangs are not dunes: partial relationship)

sources.label: Wang et al. 2016 review, Qaidam Basin as a Mars analogue (Earth-Science Reviews, as surfaced by search)
Meng et al. 2024, Deep learning selection of analogues for Mars landing sites in the Qaidam Basin

sites.limitations: Altitude 2.7-3 km makes air temperature low relative to latitude. Yardangs are an erosional, not depositional, aeolian landform; the AEOLIAN pair is weaker than the CHLORIDE pair.

sites.name: White Sands gypsum dune field
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Gypsum dunes fed by seasonal evaporation of Lake Lucero; arid.

pairs.relationship: Analog to sulfate-rich eolian outcrops at Meridiani Planum

sources.label: White Sands gypsum dunes as an analog to sulfate-rich eolian outcrops at Meridiani Planum (Geology 2006, as surfaced by search)

sites.limitations: Gypsum (sulfate) dunes, not basaltic dunes; Martian dark dunes are basaltic. Climate warmer than Mars.

sites.name: Jingpo Lake volcanic field
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Basaltic lava field with tubes and pit craters; humid-continental forested climate.

pairs.relationship: Proposed in a review as terrestrial analog for the Marius Hills region
same proposal; mare relation indirect

sources.label: Lunar lava tube base construction / terrestrial test-site reviews (as surfaced by search; specific attribution unverified)

sites.limitations: Attribution of the proposal not verified by opening the paper; forested climate unlike the Moon. Kept as exploratory.
sites.eligibility_reason: support not verified by primary source; humid forested climate

sites.name: Manjanggul lava tube, Jeju
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Basaltic island, well-known lava tube; humid subtropical climate.

pairs.relationship: Cited as a well-known Asian lava-tube example; a review notes it lacks the full surface-to-subsurface sequence for rille formation

sources.label: Lunar lava tube base construction / terrestrial test-site reviews (as surfaced by search; specific attribution unverified)

sites.limitations: Source states a limitation; humid climate. Kept as exploratory.
sites.eligibility_reason: source notes the analogy is incomplete; not verified by primary source

sites.name: Black Point lava flow, San Francisco Volcanic Field
sites.coordinate_source: approximate centroid (general geographic knowledge, not from the cited paper)
sites.environmental_characteristics: Basaltic cinder/lava terrain, semi-arid high desert.

pairs.relationship: NASA page caption: used to test a lunar electric rover

sources.label: NASA Science - Planetary Analogs
